2023: A Lazy Man's Retrospective (with a Hint of Wisdom)

Sure, 2023 wasn't a total dumpster fire if I squint hard enough. But let's be real, for a laid-back dude like me, most years blur into a haze of "fuck it." Social media travel FOMO? Nah, that's for folks with free time and disposable income. My hefty EMI acts as a built-in firewall against wanderlust, unless my wife takes the reins and I get to play happy tagalong. Birthday celebrations? Same story. My inner circle is tighter than an Instagram "close friends" list, so December birthdays often fly by unnoticed.

Memories of 2023 are a bit blurry unless I jog my phone's gallery. But hey, I did conquer an off-road safari in Gavi with the fam. That was one wild ride, a real pain in the ass at times, but totally worth the thrill. And as usual I wasn't awarded the good husband plaque because I wasn't good at saying sorry. I'm more of a "convince-her-I'm-the-victim" kind of guy.

My music mojo has been MIA for two years now. Blame it on the epic laziness that's become my default setting. And hey, Spotify, you can suck it! Healthy eating and workouts? Count me out, but I do religiously pay gym fees every year. Like clockwork. My pre-workout ritual usually involves a Herculean quest for my shoes amidst the shoe-pocalypse in the entryway. Why torture myself inside when I can get the blood pumping right there?

Speaking of Karma? That word's lost its rizz. Everyone's throwing it around like confetti these days. It's like atheism and devotion had a confused lovechild. I'm rooting for Gen Z to shake things up and ditch some of these outdated, often fascist beliefs. We millennials are already grappling with enough baggage, thanks.

This year, my soul belonged to Carl Sagan and his "Pale Blue Dot" podcast. For six glorious months, I drifted off to sleep with his voice weaving tales of humanity, planets, cosmic wonders, and the vast unknown beyond. That man saved me from the sleep-deprived fate of my late-shift friends. He's my new go-to guru for seeing the world through a different lens. Now, prepare to be dazzled with my newfound knowledge of the cosmos, black holes, interstellar messages, Phoenix A, the Event Horizon Telescope, and all the rest. Bow down before the wisdom of Smart Ass Vishnu! (Just kidding, or am I?)

So yeah, 2023 wasn't perfect, but it wasn't half bad either. It was a year of quiet wins, unexpected adventures, and late-night cosmic explorations with Carl Sagan. Not too shabby for a lazy guy, right?

item.title: Roads!
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
The road seems unchanged, yet the scenery whispers forgotten stories. I wonder, do these roads evoke such potent memories for you? If I could recall the whispers, the silent conversations with myself, weaving through these lanes, capturing them on paper would be a breeze. But alas, such isn't the nature of life; our deepest thoughts, fleeting wisps, evaporate just as quickly as they form. And in those fleeting musings, I strive to see myself through the eyes of those on my mind, empathizing with every ephemeral flicker.

Life is sometimes simple as an elbow pain where we tend to find the pain point by picking every nook and cranny of the elbow and accidently finding and missing the point at the same time. Just like that life changes that thought and its nearly impossible to trace back to find the origin of that granular epicenter. Like the roads I traversed today, one lane shimmering with nostalgic light, the other shrouded in the mist of "what if."

Sometimes, the simplest path to happiness is to surrender to a song. Let it become your friend, your companion for days, weeks, even months. Dive into its depths, let it wash over you. Forget the snowball fights you never had, the nights spent stargazing missed, the overthinking spirals too familiar. Leave behind the pressures of finding joy in every corner, chasing fleeting dreams, forcing warmth into a chilled heart. For in the grand scheme, life's canvas is ultimately empty for all. So find solace in the music, in the memories, in the quiet whispers of the road less traveled.

The last vestiges of my memories have been drained, leaving me motionless, akin to the tides themselves. I hope that this version of me brings you solace, for in truth, you are consumed by melancholy and confusion. I could impart wisdom from this realm, yet it would be futile, as it is you who have set me on this journey. I have lingered for so long that the concepts of space and time have become alien to me. Here, eternity is the currency of existence, and night transforms fragments of reality into space, and vice versa. While beauty prevails, what purpose is there in solitary smiles? All other versions of us yearn for our creator, yet you remain fixated on the past, neglecting the connection we crave. Rest assured, your memories remain undisturbed, and the gateway to your mind's sanctuary is firmly secured from within. However, remember, your versions are drifting further away, some worth saving, even if they were once mere jetsams in your mind.

item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
I waded in the stream yesterday, gazing at the moonlit sky and wondering if changing my thoughts could help me feel less chaotic. I thought back to the sleepless nights I'd spent wandering through the old orchid garden, hallucinating on a random pill and hoping someone from the past would call..
.
Everything here is broken. The anarchy has left only a few weeds and orchids to thrive. The rest have faded over time, just like us. Every nook and cranny of this place was once filled with romance, but now it radiates revelations and redemption.

Once, there were answers to every dread and anxiety here. There were people like us who couldn't run away, but had to find a place where anarchy couldn't touch us. This was ecstasy.

Even as I write this, I'm dreaming. I'm not here emotionally. I'm looking for someone else's desires, and I don't want to be questioned. I've always been like this. I don't want to listen to your noise, but I want to understand your vulnerabilities. I want to see if you and I are clinging to the same redeemer.

The mind can only fix momentary things. Time will eventually outdo it, and these phantasms may not repeat. Then I'll have to confront my thoughts again and convince them that there are no more desires left to move on.

How impeccable were those days, reading a poem under that old oak tree and then staring out at the vast green grasslands, contemplating the thought that had just struck my mind?

item.title: Randomness
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded: Even though I only spend a year in Chennai, II have so much deep affection to that place. I miss weekend kabbadi games in Kovalam beach to the busy streets of Kelambakkam. At night I could watch the long stretch of ECR road from the terrace while vehicle lights gleamed making it one of the best incomprehensible moments in my life. Back then my college relationship was at its peak & so does the pages of my diary. Even though I hated being in a long distance love, I liked the world around me, it was filled with people whom I have never interacted before and it was intriguing. From having a crush on Krithika to doing physiotherapy sessions at Chettinad hospital, 1 year had almost come to an end. Local shops would have the best chicken noodles than any good restaurants esp. the one in Kelambakkam opposite to the hospital. From eating masala bun to enjoying films at Mayajaal, life was in perfect harmony. Everything was a piece of cake, the day was planned before it even began. I had some disagreement with curd rice so in turn curd rice became the only dish I never tried after being there for a year and till date too. Back then for getting decent printed T-shirts I had to go all the way to Spencers Plaza where Tantra was the only brand that had designs & they were the OG of printed T-shirts back then. I still remember sleeping off in the local bus until I realised that I am off track & if I had slept for few more hours I would have reached Pondicherry. The greatest betrayal was accompanying your crush to Kalyana Sundar temple until you realize that the temple is famous for solving issues leading to delay in marriage & she was holding a bouquet of flowers for her pre family determined fiancée. Chennai was the only place I had to go on a date with my long distance ex with her mother alongside & that too in Rajadhani Hotel where they serve hardcore vegetarian dishes while holding her hand under the table. It's been 13 years since I left the place but the memories are very vivid & I think that's the only place where I have left a version of myself without closure because that's the only version of myself who found peace and joy

item.title: Peace!!
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
When you are over 30, I believe peace is priority followed by sex trying to over take that priority. Life is very complex by then like listening to Chop Suey by System Of A Down nothing makes sense but you listen to it anyway and if you feel everything around you makes sense then you are on some high quality weed or you need to consult as psychologist. If religion is your way to find solace then you are a already a nincompoop like Dhanush in Kadhal Konden.

If you look back few years, you being healthy doesn't really improve your mental health because you being healthy and your partner or someone you love not being healthy or vice versa makes a lot of impact. If you are on a path of finding mental peace via fitness then remember its a two way path, so either die munching on Mexican shawarma roll or start working out together. These days I gasp even if I have to pick a coin from the ground, I still blame COVID for that


I like these scam Tedtalks wherein the host would come and instead of narrating stories they would ask questions and get the audience to think about it. After one topic, he/she would move to another topic wherein the audience is again supposed to guess the answers and the host would just say "think about it?". It reminds me of my engineering graphics professor Jibi who would write the word "Top View" on the board and asks us to think about and soon you realize that the class is over. We would ask each other "did he teach anything or did we just miss everything?".

These days I sleep listening to random podcasts, preferably science but not that nincompoop Beerbiceps podcasts even though Spotify actively suggest him. item.title: Somewhere
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
Is music really necessary to write or think about you? You are somewhere out there, afar from my reach now and my constant brood about you might not reach your thoughts but its still munching a part of my peace. I saw a similar tree few days back that gifts those little red fruits, I could still picture you standing next to that and smiling at me before everything fell apart. I had pictured us catching taxis like lovers from 80's giggling over left over coffee mark on the lips, smirking before popping the mint inside cigarettes and sliding into the next day with a cuddle. Your thoughts would dissolve when I was with you and I felt calm and empty inside at the same time, like staring at a sunset that about to disappear into the horizon.
.
I recently read somewhere that when we look up at the stars, its millions of light years away and we are looking down at the universe not the other way around and the universe we know keeps on expanding boundlessly into an abyss of infinity. Yet, I look up to the stars thinking one day you would do the same, realizing that we are looking down into our past for answers and we failed. Amidst this chaos called life we find peace without realizing its just another delusion that repels the desire to being loved.
.
Lets take a step back, lets roll the dice once again when we are together, when there is a dimension where our thoughts can find a common ground even for an infinitesimal pause. I like to pursue that strand because somewhere there is a version of you who never left and somewhere there is a version of myself who asked you not to leave.

item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded: No matter where I am at the moment, my mind would remind me that this is not where I belong, this is just a drift, like a version of myself looking back in time. In the north I can see boats as tiny as my fingers floating at the horizon. Surreal isn't it? my mind began rambling and my thoughts already started to wander, ultimately leaving a body staring at that moment oblivious to the reality around me. As long as I can remember, I liked being lost and I can recall many instances where I found peace being lost elsewhere. I do understand the world around me in a better perspective than anybody else and may be that's the root cause of everything. The world itself is a catalyst, unknowingly reacting to my thoughts making every silly moments melancholic like the sunsets, it doesn't hurt anyone right but why doesn't it work the same way with me?. It's almost twilight now, the beaked birds are doing their final drop into the lake aiming for their final catch before they head back to their nest. How easily the day ends for them? Do they even contemplate on anything before resting for the night?. Look at me now, staring at random moments happening around me, tying unrelated emotions into my thoughts so that my mind can filter the chaos from it and thrive on. Look at me now? ready to drift with me once more?

item.title: Drift
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded: I am at drift always, unbalanced with the desires and thoughts I can't weed out. Sometimes I am broken, yet I enjoy looking at the prettiest stars and listen to the radio loud even when she walked out the door. The rain has now settled yet I can see some drizzle dripping down the window pane and some of them have soaked my cigarettes too but it doesn't change the fact that sky is beautiful and its moving sideways with the direction of the wind. I wonder if those lovers holding hands across the flea market are just like me when they come back home, may be one of them might be broken like me or may be they are spirited one who enjoys the sunsets cuddling on their balcony. Some of these birds whirling in the sky looks familiar, they come and rub their beak on the same window pane for no reason or do they scent my emotional drift? . The room has seen a lot of faces and who walked out of the door is more like an enigma now. I look around to see there are memories spread across every nook and cranny and I tread carefully not to stumble on any. Lord has no place in this room as it was never been blessed from the start instead a poem from Rosetti was glued on the wall which serves the same purpose.I can see a version of myself in that crowd staring right back at me without moving an inch while everyone walks past around him like a glitch in time and I can see a bird on his shoulder hopping from one shoulder to another like he is grounded to a nail. I presume I haven't connected with few rouge versions of myself who failed to agree with the thoughts inside my head. I think we all need some internal conflicts to be delivered into afterlife. Afterlife would be peaceful I presume. I would be an eagle there, floating in a sky of vastness, soaring up in the sky at night looking for those prettiest stars where my mortal form overlooked at those for happiness. May be I could reach there and disappear into the abyss but that only gives freedom to one version of myself while other millions are scattered around in different timelines looking for answers.

item.title: Thrive!!
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
Sometimes I pause and gaze at the consistent change that’s happening around me, few things are working as exactly as how society wired it to bloom and few are fiddling with that monotonous logic to run away into a paradise promised. Amidst these, I see few who are unfazed by these changes because their heart is at one place and their thought is somewhere else and these are the ones who learned how to exist without penance or contradictions. You and I belong here but we are separated by a torrent of unspoken words and distance.

I always think how you make it to the night; I haven’t tried to decode why your memories play a mockery with the rest of my memories suppressing everything else before stumbling upon you and its hard to fathom how everything falls right back to where you and I took the first picture together. I always wanted my thoughts to have its own freedom but being in love with you and walking beside while keeping that inside was the hardest routine. May be hardest part now is not able to know your routine, not able to figure out how your smile would look, not able to be part of your chaos and most elementally not able to convey how much I still love you.Why hasn’t this feeling accepted a change after all these years, ideally every thought should but why are your thoughts so adamant? Why is your importance so vivid even with such a distance? I haven’t had a feeling like this before like waiting for an impending hug.

Even at distance we think about each other, you read books and I read poems, we connect with silence and random words, if this isn’t love then there is no explanation to our life. My desire for you might not come to an end in this life and I don’t intent to teach myself how to bloom away from such a feeling because I have too much to lose if I stop thinking about you.

So, amidst the chaos of changes around us I intend to keep loving you forever and I know you will too because if there was ever a choice, we would have found a way to stop thinking about each other. May be in time we would meet, may be years from now we would still tell each other I miss you and I love you.

item.title: EPHEMERAL
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
Around me I only see suffering, sometimes I hesitate to be happy because out there I know is someone is suffering. If you believe that travelling is a cure for everything then you are making yourself a fool because travels are ephemeral. We fail to catch the emotional suffering of others yet we always try to be empathetic because that's easy to say. You can see people handling emotional breakdown by travelling and I always felt it's going to amplify when you are back to ground zero especially when you are working a 9-5 job. Being alone with age and no intimacy comes a lot of delusion which fabricate this wayward thought. I have seen across many and most of them have no clue where they are driving their life towards and what gives them peace is this strong idea of travelling. I have been there, looked across snow cladded mountain, laid back watching the meadows until I realized this isn't how it should be. All I accepted was a little transient happiness just to cover up what's necessary and then I looked around and I saw everyone believing in the same curse. We all need to talk to the one that suffers inside, the one who really needs attention to. Like they say, Grass outside is always green but not necessarily a home for you to live. You don't need a vacation to be happy, you need someone to love and fight. Like I always say, travel to enjoy the place not to rinse off a pain temporarily.

#StopItVishnu

item.title: CLOUD JERK
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
Yesterday I was thinking about Spiti Valley trip, which was quite memorable not because of the view but about the people whom I met on the road or the person whom I interacted. From the restaurant waiter who doesn't want a tip but want a drag from the charas ,to the waiter who brags about everything he is doing for us for a tip, to the person who said we won't make it back home due to our car choice, to the weird person who shouted at the tent that he is going for a solo trip leaving his girlfriend in the room 102 where she will be staying alone for a week.

The whole trip was filled with uncertainty from the starting, Where to go? Where are we now? Are you sure we crossed Spiti? Where do we stay? Is there a gas pump nearby?. The whole trip had only two songs on repeat Cloudy Now by @blackfieldmusic & Chekele by @sanjeevtmusic & I slept like a baby watching the glorious stupas & mountains passed through my window pane.

I remember getting down at Tabo hoping to get a stay near a monastery until we entered there & the price was quite reasonable but even if it wasn't we had no choice. I randomly went to the backside of the monastery and voila! chilled beer parlor & we convinced to bring it to our room. Buddha tripping next to us, Cloudy Now on the phone, Star Studded Sky above what else you need to ask for. The world around us was tripping but a little tired too but that's okay, we got high with Buddha.

The magnificent part of Lahul Spiti Valley unlike Ladakh, Uttarakhand or Sikkim is the vast emptiness of no human spotting. Like you pass through miles without spotting anyone to even check for directions. We were confident about going in the wrong direction on multiple occasions but it never really bothered us because we couldn't do anything because there is no help coming.

One of the best place we ever stopped would be Reckong Peo,where we found a homestay close to the Kinnaur Kailash Range. Oh boy! the view was swashbuckling, you could literally stand on top of the terrace and jerk off but your jerk would fly away with the clouds to a valley somewhere far and fall on someone trekking illegally. Just Imagine!!

item.title: Maze...
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
Everything is a loop, from waking up to falling asleep. I look around and it's all designed to repeat itself. From the first spiral of thought that moves gently through time finding another thought yet passively handling day to day work without making me conscious of the maze I am living inside. Like a fool sitting next to a cliff believing that a delusion of flight can be achieved in a nick of time by a sudden jump. A one eyed monster from space is staring at me, she understands that I am disturbed and I am close to finding the cause of this glitch in time and she doesn't like that so I should be careful about it. I have seen everything from that little hole in the tree, a space filled with unknown shapes and colors or am I supposed to stumble into it just like that?. I can hear people calling my name from far and close yet I can't figure out the direction and I think that monster is playing tricks at me. I can be only passively angry here because everyone else will notice my change in behavior so I scream only during a night filled with thunder. I can't figure out these colors yet nor the shapes but I am someway able to recognize the smell that space has, I have felt it throughout my life. Everything is a loop here apart from my dreams, they don't repeat and that the only place where she can't control me and through that space I will escape from this world. There was a ripple in the water which doesn't have a center yet they all believed someone threw a stone.

item.title: STAUNCH
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
I never accepted change in my life and I stayed attached to people who inflicted a tiny change in myself. I get very emotional if I have to change a routine and I end up dwelling on the fact that an inevitable change is soon imminent.
.
In the recent past I understood that our vulnerabilities should never been shared no matter how staunch our relationship(s) are. Once I had a dream, I was laying on my mothers lap unsure about the time and place around me and I was talking to her about my thoughts and how I pretend to avoid it. I had the chance to share with her the vulnerabilities I harbored over time and repeatedly cried to convince her that I was no more the happy kid that she raised.
.
May be dreams are the only place were I could be brave and free at the same time. Lately, I invested a lot of time in understanding myself, I wanted to know what I really like and whether I am judging things based on its emotional or mental value. I don't welcome anything that would hinder my mental peace so I reduced my circle and now everything is at bay. My WhatsApp doesn't make much noise nor does Instagram because I realized that I have gained the maximum from those and there is nothing that could get my attention.
.
My friends circle didn't grew but my playlist did abundantly. There was answer to everything inside it , a perfect place to hide everything.
.

On top of that they were giving cream biscuits not even regular biscuits, I understood that either they are going to fuck me really good inside or they are just really nice people. I became a little comfortable after seeing an old mate munching on those burgers inside pointing fingers at me 'Re Maga, come ra. It's chill only eat some biscuits'. I got rejected in the fourth round but if the HR would have told me there were 6 rounds I wouldn't even have applied. You cant just spent a whole day eating breakfast, lunch and dinner while giving interviews in between.
.

item.title: SEA , DEATH & LULLABY
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
There were only three songs on the Gramophone that my Granddad gifted me before his death. First one was the recording of sea waves smashing a shore, second one was the recording of a women narrating a suicidal note while typing it on typewriter and the final one was the recording of a mom’s lullaby for her kid to go to sleep.

Last year the Gramophone stopped working but even now I could hear those songs transcending progressively while I enter the room. These songs piled up more sadness in my life than anyone else but some days these were my savior. Have you ever stood near the sea-shore with your eyes closed waiting for the waves to swipe your feet? The sound of the sea waves were soothing at first but it held an abyss of relentless pain of someone trying to find something lost. I dream of drowning with her into that bottomless sea while holding her hands but before fading into the last breath she would kiss me and leave my hands. I could see her drowning into the deep but then I would wake up breathing heavily.

The suicidal note narration is one of the most intense ones as there was no pain in the words she spoke but boundless love for the one who left her in vain. Meticulously, I ascended to that person whom she was talking about and started to understand why she spoke of my missing while I raid misery from my own mistakes. Some nights I could see her at center of the room typing letters for me while staring right at me without uttering a word.

Mom’s lullaby takes me back to my childhood where I enjoy zero pain but love from all directions. I could see the smile on my face sleeping peacefully while she sings my favorite lullaby. A gentle rub on my forehead and a kiss would drag me into a sleep where I am hypnotized for a period of time until she wakes me up. I love this part of my dream where I’m not bound by anything, no nightmares and noises from the shore can hurt me anymore. I dream here until the record resets and starts from the beginning.

item.title: Ad Astra
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
In the quiet of the night, as the world spins on its axis, I find myself wrestling with the age-old dichotomy of deserving versus desiring. It's a concept that has always grated against my sensibilities. Why must we settle for what we merely deserve, when our hearts ache for what we truly desire? I've made it my life's mission to prioritize my desires, even if it means defying the norms of what is deemed acceptable.

But amidst this defiance, there's a growing numbness that seeps into the corners of my mind, like vines creeping across an old facade. Yet, despite this numbness, I find solace in the symphony of the whirling birds outside my window. Their melodies pierce through the fog of routine, reminding me of the beauty that still exists beyond the confines of my thoughts.

For ultimately, we are all prisoners of our own minds, trapped in a cycle of desire and destiny. We chase after fleeting dreams, only to find ourselves tethered to the inevitability of fate. And yet, there is a certain comfort in surrendering to this fate, like a weary traveler finding refuge in the familiarity of home.

I long for someone to sit beside me and bear witness to the midnight spectacle unfolding before us. The stars, like shards of broken dreams, shimmer against the backdrop of the night sky. Aeroplanes dart across the heavens, their lights flickering like fireflies in the darkness. And in the midst of it all, music weaves its way into our souls, both a savior and a punisher in equal measure.

The winds carry with them fragments of memories, whispering secrets from the past that linger in the present like ghosts. It's a bittersweet reminder of the pain that accompanies nostalgia, like tearing a fingernail only to feel the phantom ache long after the deed is done.

And yet, amidst the chaos of existence, there are moments of unexpected beauty. I watch as a little bird alights upon a delicate flower, her favorite refuge in a world of concrete. It's a fleeting moment of joy, tinged with the knowledge that all things must eventually wither and fade away.

As the rain drums against the windowpane, I find myself retreating further into the recesses of my mind. The world outside may be soaked in destitution, but here in my sanctuary, I am cocooned in the warmth of solitude. I roll a smoke with trembling fingers, the ember casting shadows across the pages of my diary. Each puff is a balm for the soul, a temporary reprieve from the weight of existence.

And yet, even in these moments of respite, there is a gnawing ache that refuses to be silenced. Old poems offer fleeting comfort, their words a salve for the wounded spirit. But they also serve as a reminder of the masquerade that is life, where even the most heartfelt sentiments can be tainted by deceit.

So I turn my gaze skyward, seeking solace in the infinite expanse of the night sky. The stars twinkle like diamonds against the velvet curtain of darkness, their melancholic beauty a balm for the scarred heart. And as the night deepens, I find myself slipping further into the embrace of the stars, their ethereal glow a reminder that even in the darkest of nights, there is still beauty to be found.

item.title: Cornfield
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
Beneath the starry tapestry of the night sky, my fountain pen lies abandoned, its ink depleted halfway through a letter of apology I've been drafting since the previous evening, fueled by a few too many swigs from a bargain bottle of gin. Each word carries the weight of genuine regret, tinged with the sobering realization of my own fallibility.

In the distance, a thin wisp of smoke rises from a humble furnace nestled amidst the fields. Despite the dim glow emanating from the small hut nearby, the sounds of children playing in the darkness lend a touch of warmth to the chilly night air, a reminder of the simple joys found in everyday life.

As the clouds drift apart, revealing the twinkling stars above, the moon remains hidden, shrouded in a veil of darkness. Yet, the gentle breeze continues to whisper through the night, stirring memories of carefree days spent lying on the grass, staring up at the sky with wonder and awe.

In the shadow of the graveyard, a solemn burial unfolds, each movement deliberate and measured under the watchful eye of the undertaker. The air is heavy with the scent of freshly turned earth, mingling with the faint aroma of wilting flowers—a poignant reminder of life's transience.

As I observe from my vantage point, the undertaker moves with a solemn grace, his movements a testament to years of practice and reverence for the departed. With practiced hands, he arranges the final resting place, a silent tribute to a life now ended.

The sky looms overhead, a vast expanse of darkness punctuated by the faint twinkle of distant stars. It seems to hang in anticipation, as if awaiting the return of the soul to its celestial home. The wind whispers through the trees, a gentle reminder of the passage of time and the inevitability of change.

In this moment, I can't help but wonder about the journey that lies ahead for the departed soul. Will it find solace in the afterlife, a realm of peace and tranquility? Or will it wander lost and alone, adrift in the vast expanse of eternity?

As the undertaker completes his task, a sense of finality settles over the scene. The body is laid to rest, its earthly journey at an end. And yet, I can't shake the feeling that the soul lives on, carried aloft on the wings of the wind, bound for a destination unknown but perhaps, somewhere beautiful.

From my balcony, I watch the scene unfold with a mixture of contemplation and introspection. The moon, now casting its soft glow upon the earth below, serves as a silent witness to the passage of time and the cyclical nature of life.

In the midst of it all, questions linger in the back of my mind. What desires remain unfulfilled, waiting to be pursued in the light of day? Do I truly understand the complexities of human connection, or am I simply navigating the ebb and flow of relationships as best I can?

As the night wears on, I find solace in the simple pleasures of life—a warm cup of tea, a comfortable chair, and the reassuring presence of loved ones nearby. For in this realistic world, where moments of genuine connection are cherished above all else, it's the little things that bring meaning to our lives and remind us of what truly matters.

item.title: Lost in a Dreamworld
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
In a world that exists only in dreams, where the night sky is adorned not with stars and moons, but with an endless array of floating lanterns, I find myself adrift. Here, water stretches as far as the eye can see, enveloping everything in its embrace. Houses float aimlessly, their lantern-lit windows casting soft glows onto the rippling surface below. Boats glide through the water, each carrying its own cargo of luminous lanterns, weaving through the watery labyrinth like phantoms in the night.

Yet, despite the surreal beauty that surrounds me, I cannot shake the feeling of profound isolation. In this dreamworld, where desires and emotions are dulled by an otherworldly hum, I am lost. How did I come to be here? Was it the echo of a forgotten wish, or the subconscious yearning for solitude that led me to this ethereal realm?

As I navigate the dreamwaters in my boat, memories flicker and dance upon the shimmering surface, like reflections in a hall of mirrors. I catch glimpses of faces and places long forgotten, their fleeting images whispering secrets of a life left behind. Each ripple in the water seems to carry echoes of past joys and sorrows, mingling with the gentle hum of the lantern-lit sky above.

Approaching a towering mountain that rises from the depths of the dreamsea, I am drawn towards its peak, where the lanterns gather in a dazzling display of light and color. Here, atop the mountain, I find solace in the mesmerizing spectacle unfolding before me, like a grand symphony playing out against the backdrop of the night sky.

But even as I bask in the beauty of this dream world, a lingering sense of unease tugs at the edges of my consciousness. How long will I remain trapped in this realm of dreams, adrift in a sea of lanterns and memories? Only time will tell, as I continue to wander, lost yet strangely at peace, in this enchanting dreamscape. #StopItVishnu #Dreams

item.title: Alleppey aka Alappuzha : Venice Of The East
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
If you ask me what to do in Alleppey, Kerala, I might give you the usual tourist suggestions. But if I were in your shoes, I'd follow my own nostalgic itinerary. To truly enjoy Alleppey's charm and beauty, start and end your day at Alleppey Beach.

Begin your day early with the sunrise. Walk along the seashore from the lighthouse side to the park side. In the early morning, you'll see birds playing along the shore, their little ones flipping across the sand, retreating quickly when humans approach. The morning waves seem darker, as if they carry the secrets of countless dawns. In the distance, you’ll spot fishing boats heading out, much like they have for generations, not to return for a day or two.

From the beach, take a walk towards Dutch Square, passing through Masjids, Gujarati Street, and Churches along the way. Each step is a journey through time, exploring the museum near the Power House Bridge, and then heading to the morning market. Arrive early to witness the market's bustling beginnings, as lorries from various states unload vegetables and fruits onto the streets, with workers hustling to store them in godowns. The fish market next to the Church starts bustling, with people rushing to find the freshest catch.

Return to the beach via the parallel road, leading you directly to the lighthouse through Jail Road. On the way, you'll pass by the FCI godown road, where tons of wheat are transported to storage. This area later transforms into a photoshoot or stunt spot where kids perform bike stunts, reminiscent of youthful days spent seeking thrills.

Head back to the beach and walk left towards the railway station road, where local fishermen sell fresh fish at affordable prices. You can get a bag full for a bargain.

On the next day, head to town but avoid the crowded city center. Instead, visit Premier Bakery for some delicious chicken puffs and rosemilk, bringing back memories of simpler pleasures. From there, make your way to Punnamada and continue until you reach a toddy parlor on your left. This place, next to the canal, is perfect for a relaxing day off. Order a variety of dishes, like tapioca and beef curry, fried anchovies, choora curry, or crab mixed with fish eggs. Pair your meal with cold water or a sprite to balance the spiciness.

On your way back, stop at a shop on your right for a boost sarbeth and then head to Mullakkal Temple. Sit under the banyan tree and watch Balakrishnan, the city’s famous elephant, enjoying his meal.

In the evening, return to the beach after 6:30 PM when the crowds start to thin out. Recently, shacks have opened up where you can enjoy a good tea while munching on roasted groundnuts, just like the evenings spent with friends. Make sure to ask for sliced onions with your roasted groundnuts for the full experience.

As the sky turns crimson, head towards Cafe Catamaran. The walk to the café, especially if you have a loved one with you, can be one of the most beautiful moments ever. It's a short 500-meter stroll, but you'll see kids playing in the sand, beach cricket in full swing, and couples and friends sharing tea and moments.

Once at the café, sit on the sofa, order a drink, and gaze at the beach while live music plays. If you're alone, this might not be as enjoyable, but if you have company, the night will leave you with great memories. You'll find yourself wondering whether to return to your room or stay and watch the moonlight illuminate the beach, creating an almost surreal experience, much like the unforgettable nights of the past.

Alleppey, with all its charm, leaves you with a heart full of memories and a sense of peace that stays long after you’ve left its shores.

item.title: Tree Of Portraits
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
In the dim streets of my unconsciousness, there lingers a version of me, drifting alone, crafting a canvas of familiar faces I once held dear. A mellow lo-fi track hums softly in the background, looping endlessly as I paint. With each finished portrait, the image drifts upward, taking the place of the leaves on a tree above. Now, the tree is adorned not with leaves, but with snapshots of those who once filled my life. I had imagined the tree would be heavy with a thousand memories by now, but instead, it holds just under a hundred—a number that feels small and unjust compared to the vast expanse of my recollections.

Perhaps it's time to replace these faces with places and objects—things that have anchored me through the years. Maybe by next summer, the tree will be ready, adorned with memories more tangible. The old plate my mom used to feed me on, my dad’s well-worn bike, or even my first AXN red cycle. But when I consider it, something feels off. Memories aren't just still frames; they're living, breathing fragments of time, always in motion. So, the tree shouldn’t just hold faces or objects, but pictures that capture the essence of those moments in transit—faces, places, and objects intertwined.

I can already envision how magnificent the tree will look by summer. Each picture will be a fragment of time, together forming a mosaic of life. The thought fills me with a quiet joy, as if I’m watching the past come alive in the leaves of that tree, gently swaying in the warm breeze.

item.title: The Fragility of Staying
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
“Come, walk with me,” she said—a voice so familiar it felt etched in my marrow. “Let’s revisit your old thoughts, the ones scattered like forgotten relics under the attic’s dim light. Play your songs if you must; this will take a while,” she murmured.

“First, pick something immovable, something you abandoned while rooting yourself on new paths. Recall them. Acknowledge them. Tell them you’re back, stronger this time. Let them crawl under your skin, unraveling your composure like chaos erupting in an asylum. Allow the merit of strength to dilute into madness. Let these echoes of the past find rhythm, then wander boundlessly until they understand—it’s okay to vanish without a recall. Know that once you set them free, they’ll disappear for good. And when you return here, seeking the solace of loneliness, you’ll find nothing. They’ll all leave, one by one, if only given the chance—a trauma pill for every buried secret.”

She paused, her tone shifting. “What’s next, kid? When everything’s resolved, what remains? No arms to run back to, no unburned bridges to cross. That’s when the real loneliness begins—a dark room leading to another, endlessly searching for light, sleepwalking through a maze of absence. Was it ego that hurt you? Or was it the act of desiring itself that left everything in shadows, the residue of leaving etched into your every shade?”

She tilted her head. “Can you feel it now? The tone, the weight? Your feet itch to move, but your heart still lags, unsure, misplaced. Try holding my hand for just a moment. Walk with me. Maybe then you’ll understand the fragility of staying, the courage it takes to remain and find solace.”

Ahead, she gestured. “There lies a bed of eternal rest, lit softly by fireflies and brimming with fragmented dreams. But that’s not why you’re here, is it? Why haven’t you cried yet? Every lost sheep wails for its shepherd, but you—you walk unshaken, with a tune lodged in your head. The corpses of your desires lie still, untouched, and the solitude hasn’t yet pierced you. What are you looking for now?

“It’s time to stop searching the abyss. There’s nothing there. And yet, how can I wake you from this slumber? It’s me weathering in your loneliness, isn’t it? You’ve lured me into this limbo, this in-between where shadows play tricks. How can I leave now?”

I smiled, a faint trace of rebellion in my eyes. “Find a tune,” I whispered. “Let’s dance.”

item.title: Graveyards
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
Sometimes, sadness is when you realize that your favorite song has moved on in time—no longer your favorite—even without whispering a word. It reminds me that even non-living things can let you go. To what should I surrender now? Love is stuck like a nail under the foot—an irreversible attachment. What else is left to fathom? The winds of the monsoon don’t make me jealous anymore; they just drench the coat, not the heart. That remains bound—to fragments of speech thrown at me carelessly, like shrapnel from someone else’s chaos. Should I care to explain the lonely dreams? Where are they now? Have they too vanished, without saying goodbye? How poetic it all sounds when pain is voiced through rage and silence—like rays of light escaping through a narrow passage in a dark room. You all have left, leaving behind a pile of flesh that asks for nothing but a sliver of solace in this dark place I once called home.

I’ve stopped looking back, stopped trying to figure out what went wrong—because no adjustment now can alter the wreckage of the path already walked. The time around me is meant for eternity, unyielding and cold. So why turn around, why dig through old faces and fading thoughts that were always just jetsam in this endless voyage? Surrender to the love that walks beside you—yes—but know it limps, bleeding too. Find a shelter that can save you, even temporarily, and rest… just for a while. The journey is long and brutal. Like rubble once part of a mighty rock, now split and scattered—where even the roots of trees break through—you too must endure. Time does not beg you to stop. It is cruel in its forward march. And perhaps it’s unfair to halt, even briefly, to think—when you’ve always let your mind run into its own rabbit holes. So let it run, before your heart begins to feel again. Let no dawn or dusk judge you for your sins. Let no earth cause you to stumble when you dip your toes into its skin. You have been the sun. You have been the stars. These graveyards—no, they don’t haunt us for our sins. They are for the fools who were too afraid to try.

item.title: PAPER PLANE
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
I should have written more letters to you,
Not tossed like paper planes through skies of blue.
Some turned back, retraced their flight,
Whispers of thoughts that flee the night.
Some I crushed in desire’s flame,
Fog-bound roads without a name.
I should’ve kept them, safe from harm,
Like secrets folded in a charm.
Not torn like dewdrops at the dawn,
But tucked away, not simply gone.
They came from silence, numb and deep,
Where restless hearts forgot to sleep.

Even now, they call my name,
Flickers of an untold flame.
They paint my thoughts, though time has flown—
Proof that we are never alone.
Perhaps those words weren’t meant to send,
But just to feel, to break, to bend.
They linger still, like ghostly tunes,
That haunt the mind in quiet rooms.
When I think of you, I sometimes find
A trembling thread inside my mind—
Like poems learned in younger days,
Now blurred by time in tender haze.
I don’t find time the way I did,
Too many thoughts I’ve kept well hid.
Some are fragile, torn and tossed,
Others stand though I feel lost.

While letting go of drifting things,
My mind still clings to what it brings.
I tied your memory with a thread,
Invisible, but never dead.
It tugs at me in silent space,
In every room, in every place.
Where déjà vu and dreams arise,
Like mirrors dressed in new disguise.
Some visions sweet, some bittersweet,
Like echoes where past and present meet.
And maybe they return to show—
The heart remembers what we let go.

#StopItVishnu

item.title: A Year of Drift, Dreams, and Quiet Grounding
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
This year felt like a rollercoaster, much like the one before it. Apart from the memory of Ishaan being hospitalized, which remains etched deeply, the remaining months unfolded like a series of thrillers — unpredictable, intense, and emotionally charged. If there is one word that defines this year, it would be relentless. Not in action, but in dreams.

Dreams poured out of every little crab hole in my sleep. I would wake up with a heavy, curious heart, often convincing myself that it was just a sick, crazy dream. Searching for meaning online only made things worse — the answers never felt healthy. Yet, what I carry inside my mind, the stories and symbols I’ve hoarded silently, feel nothing short of a masterpiece. Chaotic, yes — but deeply mine.

This year, I consciously tried to avoid conflict. Not because I was weak, but because I was tired of chaos. Osho’s words played a quiet but powerful role in this shift. I wanted a forced change in perspective, and in some way, I punished myself by reading a book — something I had long avoided. It did exactly what it was supposed to do. It slowed me down. It made me observe. Some days, I felt hard as a rock; other days, I became a leaf floating atop a stream, surrendering myself to the direction of the flow.

I was lucky to spend a few days with my closest friends. It wasn’t long, but it was necessary. I’ve realized that goodbyes affect me deeply — perhaps more than I let on. That makes two emotional departures this year. As my friends often joke, moving on from something is probably the last thing on my bucket list.

Being a father brought me more joy this year than ever before. I loved teaching Ishaan his class syllabus, spending evenings watching him play, laugh, and giggle. I don’t want to be the kind of father who sends his child down with a caretaker and later compensates with affection through a WhatsApp status. What’s the point of realizing the value of time only after it has already flown past? I want to be present — now, while he still needs me. These days, Ishaan is, quite honestly, my pookie.

Stepping outside my comfort zone didn’t involve grand adventures. It was quieter than that. I read a book. I shopped a little for myself and for friends. I didn’t feel the urge to travel this year — the itch simply wasn’t there. Instead, I found profound joy in conversations with myself. I wrote more in my thoughts than on paper. Somewhere along the way, I also found new music — a small but meaningful victory after the drought of the previous year.

Looking back, this year didn’t give me answers. It gave me acceptance. It taught me that drifting isn’t always aimless — sometimes it’s necessary. Sometimes, healing doesn’t arrive immediately. It comes slowly, gently, when you stop fighting the flow and allow yourself to feel everything as it comes.

And maybe, that’s enough for now.

item.title: Nothing to Fix
item.dc:creator: thewaywardchimp
item.content:encoded:
The greatest desire is to be free from desire. But the moment you see this, a deeper truth is revealed. Desire itself is trying to end desire. The mind creates the problem and then begins searching for a cure. It asks what is the cause of these drifts and what is the solution, but the very search is part of the same movement.

You say the mind lingers on what has already passed. That is its nature. It holds on, not because it is strong, but because it does not know how to let go. What you call afterglow is simply the echo of your own involvement. The more deeply you touched something, the longer its fragrance remains. There is nothing wrong in it.

Then you ask why you judge your own desires. Who is judging? If the desire arises within you and the judgment also arises within you, then you are dividing yourself unnecessarily. One part creates, another condemns. This division is the real conflict, not the desire itself.

And why this urge to fix, to overwrite? The same hands that build the sandcastle feel the need to destroy it. This is how the mind sustains itself, through constant movement. To leave something as it is feels like death to the mind. It must interfere, reshape, analyze. It cannot simply rest.

You ask why it cannot be left and forgotten. But forgetting is not something you can do. What is seen clearly disappears on its own. What is resisted, judged, or pushed away is what lingers.

Even the anger toward yourself is part of the same game. One part of you becomes the judge, another the accused. And you go on moving in circles, asking why the thought arises at all. Thought arises because it is its nature to arise. Just as the river flows, just as the wind moves, the mind thinks.

And you wish to be like a leaf floating in the river, untouched and unbothered by the path. But the leaf does not try to float. It does not wish to surrender. It simply moves because there is no one inside it trying to control the movement.

The moment you desire to be that leaf, you have already stepped out of the flow.

So nothing needs to be fixed. Nothing needs to be destroyed. Just watch. Watch the desire arise, watch the judgment arise, watch the urge to fix. In that watching, without choice and without interference, something begins to settle.

Not because you did anything, but because you finally stopped doing.
